extracted.intended_audience: fanfiction authors and FanFiction.Net users (site contributors and moderators)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines and platform rules for publishing and moderating fanfiction on the FanFiction.Net website, including content ratings, banned entry types, forum rules, and moderation/privilege mechanics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Content rating system (FictionRatings)
rubrics_metrics.description: FanFiction.Net uses the content rating system from FictionRatings.com: K, K+, T, M and MA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each rating has guidance: K = general/for all ages; K+ = some violence/strong language (recommended 9+); T = PG-13 style mature themes (not for under 13); M = R-equivalent with frequent coarse language, drug use, references to sexual violence (not suitable under 16); MA = NC-17 equivalent (explicit adult content). The MA rating and explicit violent or sexual themes are forbidden on the site.

rubrics_metrics.name: MA (18+) / explicit content prohibition
rubrics_metrics.description: The MA (18+) rating is not permitted on FanFiction.Net; NC-17/explicit fiction is banned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FanFiction.Net banned NC-17 material in 2002 and no longer permits MA-rated works. The site relies on users to report inappropriately rated stories. Historical notes: previously used MPAA ratings until cease-and-desist; now uses FictionRatings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required metadata for story publishing
rubrics_metrics.description: Writers must assign a sub-category, language, and content rating when uploading stories; a short K-rated summary is required for publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stories may be published as 'Fanfiction' (one sub-category) or 'Crossover' (only two sub-categories). While a cover image is not required, the site recommends uploading one. Story titles and summaries must be rated K.

rubrics_metrics.name: Crossover rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Crossover stories may be published but may have only two assigned sub-categories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Excluding crossovers, each story gets one sub-category; crossovers are limited to two sub-categories to categorize the work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Choose-your-own-adventure and reader-insertion ban
rubrics_metrics.description: Choose-your-own-adventure (CYOA) and reader-insertion (second person/you-based) fanfiction are banned since 2005.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Official 'Entries not allowed' item #5 includes: 'Any form of interactive entry: choose your adventure, second person/you based, Q&As, etc.' The site removed all material that could insert the reader into the fiction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Songfic policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Songfics (fanfiction containing copyrighted song lyrics) are banned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Public domain lyrics (e.g., 'Amazing Grace') or lyrics written by the author are allowed; copyrighted song lyrics are not permitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lists and non-story entries not allowed
rubrics_metrics.description: Lists and other non-stories are considered disallowed content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The official Content Guideline states that lists fall under 'non-stories' along with bloopers, polls, previews, challenges, author notes, etc., and thus are not allowed on the site.

rubrics_metrics.name: Real-person fiction restriction
rubrics_metrics.description: Stories based on real-life celebrities were disallowed circa 2003.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The platform moved to prohibit real-person fiction (with some domain-specific exceptions such as professional-wrestling fanfiction being allowed in 'Miscellaneous').

rubrics_metrics.name: Copyright and trademark takedown compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: FanFiction.Net removes stories when professional authors or rights-holders request takedowns for copyrighted or trademarked works.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Numerous professional authors and producers have asked for their-based stories to be removed; the site complies with such requests and has removed works on complaint.

rubrics_metrics.name: Private messaging controls and filtering
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors can receive private messages (PMs) from affiliated accounts; authors can block users, disable PMs, and enable basic profanity filtering for incoming reviews and PMs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PMs are separated into Inbox and Outbox. There is no report button for PMs, but blocking a user stops them from leaving PMs. Authors may choose via account settings to accept or decline PMs. The site provides a profanity filter for incoming messages and reviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review moderation rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors may moderate 'anonymous reviews' (left by those not signed into an account), but cannot moderate or disable reviews left by signed-in users.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FanFiction.Net does not operate a screening or editorial board; review moderation options are limited to anonymous reviews only.

rubrics_metrics.name: Forum creation and rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors can create up to 10 personal forums and optionally link them to a category; forums must adhere to site rules and be suitable for teens.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Forum-specific rules: forums are not to be used to post stories; all discussions, language and content must be suitable for teens; the owner/moderator(s) is solely responsible for content posted within the forum.

rubrics_metrics.name: Community (custom archive) creation and moderation responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors can create or edit communities (custom archives) and hire/manage community staff who moderate entries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Community creators can hire and delete staff or stories and can check statistics detailing community popularity. Community staff moderate entries to the community archive per the creator's direction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Age requirement for registration
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Originally registration required claim of being over 18; by 2002 the limit moved down to 13. The site demographics skew young and predominantly female historically.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enforcement and policy updates (explicit/child-abuse content)
rubrics_metrics.description: FanFiction.Net enforces content policies and has taken action (including temporary shutdowns) in response to issues around explicit content and depictions of child abuse.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: FanFiction.Net experienced a temporary shutdown in July 2024 due to a policy update regarding explicit content and depictions of child abuse; the platform's hosting/registry providers have acted on content they deem violating external policies (e.g., GoDaddy deactivations noted for related sister-site content).
